speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; could you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and how they have changed since then?

Also, is the pain constant or does it flare up at specific times, and have you noticed any redness or warmth in the area?

Finally, do you have a history of gout, rheumatoid arthritis, or any recent injuries to that finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's thumb (Stener lesion) or collateral ligament injury of the fifth digit (ring finger) secondary to acute traumatic hyperextension during football.

REQUEST TEST: X-ray right hand to rule out fracture or avulsion.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
